title: Edison Invented the Bulb. He Made It Last.

beats.text: Edison invented the bulb. He made it last.

overlays.hook: Edison invented the bulb. *He made it last.*

beats.text: Born in Massachusetts in 1848, to parents who had escaped slavery in Virginia.

visual.title: Chelsea, 1848
visual.sub: son of two people who fled slavery

beats.text: At sixteen, he joined the Union Navy and served on a gunboat in the Civil War.
As an office boy at a patent law firm, he taught himself drawing, and rose to chief draftsman.
In 1876, he drew the patent drawings for Alexander Graham Bell's telephone.
In 1880, Edison's rival Hiram Maxim hired him to work on electric light.
In 1882, he patented a better way to make the carbon filament, the part that glows.

visual.caption: U.S. Patent 252,386, Process of Manufacturing Carbons, 1882

beats.text: He then supervised electric lighting installations in New York, Montreal and London.
In 1884, Edison's own company hired him as a patent expert. He wrote the standard book on electric lighting.
In 1918, he was named one of the 28 Edison Pioneers. The only Black member.
Lewis Latimer died in 1928, at 80. Edison invented the bulb. Latimer made it last.

facts.claim: Born 4 Sep 1848, Chelsea, Massachusetts; parents George and Rebecca Latimer had escaped slavery in Virginia (1842).
Enlisted in the Union Navy in 1864 at 16; landsman on the gunboat USS Massasoit.
Office boy at the Boston patent firm Crosby & Gould; learned drafting by watching; rose to chief draftsman.
Drew the patent drawings for Bell's telephone, 1876.
Hired in 1880 by Hiram Maxim's U.S. Electric Lighting Company.
U.S. Patent 252,386, Process of Manufacturing Carbons, 17 Jan 1882.
Supervised electric-lighting installations in New York, Montreal and London (Lemelson also lists Philadelphia).
Joined Edison Electric Light Co. in 1884 as draftsman and patent expert; book Incandescent Electric Lighting, 1890.
Named one of the 28 charter Edison Pioneers, 24 Jan 1918; the only Black member.
